lens: honesty and POD (cheat detection, oracle leaks, scripted decisions, POD faithfulness, LW1 door); round 3 final verification of plan_v3

findings.title: D7's goal at_config(q_home) cannot be grounded after the first replan, and its corrective loop never runs
findings.problem: (a) _build_init gives a Config fact only to current_config. move needs (Config ?q2) and plan-motion's domain needs (Config ?q2). Only compute-kin and compute-stack-kin certify Config. D7's init list, (Boxel home) (config_for_boxel q_home home), leaves out (Config q_home), although B4's matching q_clear list includes (Config q_clear). After any replan from a config other than home, no move to q_home grounds and the planner fails. In find_dice every episode replans, after a sense outcome or after a post-place registration triggers _integrity_after, so the result is 0/20 by construction. (b) _loop_done ends the holding loop as soon as the target body is held. A failed at-home test, or any plan break after the pick, therefore returns from main() without replanning. The q_readback_k renaming and the home_not_reached bound are dead code. (c) The goal is hardcoded as ('holding', target), and B3(c) has no goal keyword. (d) D7 says 'the bridge's _build_init', but G10 forbids a planner subclass and G11 forbids a hand-built init, and B3(d) lists no main-pipeline parameter that would emit these facts. (e) streams.home_config is REST_POSES under the name q_home, not DEFAULT_ARM_POS, and no package parameterises it. Each gap invites an unregistered patch (a post-loop go-home, a bridge-side init, a subclass): the scripted-motion pattern the plan exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: pddlstream_planner.py:889-890 (only current_config gets Config/at_config); domain_pddlstream.pddl:207-216; stream.pddl:12-16, 24-29, 35-40; test_full_pipeline.py:762 (goal = ('holding', target_name)), 1201-1209 (_loop_done = held_body_id == target body), 1490-1609 (a break returns to the while test); streams.py:253-258 (home_config = REST_POSES named q_home); plan D7 vs B4 init lists.
findings.required_change: Pre-register in B3(d), default off, with the B3 acceptance: a goal keyword for main(); a home-configuration parameter (joints from task_spec, symbol q_home); emission by _build_init of (Config q_home) (Boxel home) (config_for_boxel q_home home) whenever a goal configuration is declared; and, for that goal, a loop termination of 'target held AND the last move to q_home passed the at-home test', with home_not_reached as the only other exit. Replace 'the bridge's _build_init' in D7 with this parameter.

findings.title: G14 traps the executor's own IK on the executing robot, so every pick and place turns the gates red
findings.plan_location: G14, G1, G21, B7 GO criterion, D1
findings.problem: execute_pick, execute_place, execute_stack and the post-action lift call robot_utils.solve_ik on the executing robot with pc = env.client_id. solve_ik resets the 7 arm joints to the seed, then to each candidate, then back to the saved values, and every resetJointState also zeroes joint velocity. G14's closed exception list covers D9, the plan-twin mirror and the IK on the PLAN-client robot only. G14 therefore fires at the first pick, G21 marks every arm-O episode red, and B7's GO criterion cannot be met. The implementer is left to allowlist this ad hoc or to change the executor without the B3 acceptance.
findings.evidence: execution.py:1058, 1380, 1582 (pc = env.client_id); execution.py:880, 1080, 1091, 1381, 1583, 1594 (solve_ik(robot_id, ..., pc)); robot_utils.py:559-672 (resetJointState of the arm on physics_client in try/finally); G14 exceptions cite only streams.py:416-418, 470-473.
findings.required_change: Decide this now. Either (a) add to G14 and G1 a pre-registered exception for robot_utils.solve_ik's save/seed/restore on the executing robot, valid only inside a dispatcher context and asserted net-zero: positions restored bit-identically and no stepSimulation during the call, with the velocity reset disclosed as a main-pipeline property. Or (b) move execution-time IK to the plan twin under the B3 acceptance, with a BF#.

findings.title: G16 makes update_object_positions raise, but main() calls it unconditionally in Phase 1 and after every release
findings.plan_location: G16, B2 env_adapter, B3(c) oracle_phases, D9 step (5), B1(c)
findings.problem: The adapter must override update_object_positions to raise, and its counter must read 0. main() calls it at Phase 1 before the first render, after failed picks, after transit losses, after every successful place, and after stacks. execution.py calls it inside every release. B3(c)'s oracle_phases=False skips only the :576 check and Phase 4. With the override in place, main() raises before boxelization, and neither the B2 deliverable nor B7 can pass. Separately, main()'s own Phase-1 settle (50 steps) runs after D9's 50-step settle. The episode therefore does not follow the 'identical call sequence' that B1(c) probes, and D9's die-hidden assert does not happen right before the first render.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:560-564, 1734, 1845, 1906, 2085, 2153; execution.py:623; boxel_env.py:1856-1869 (getBasePositionAndOrientation on every body, the die included); map_execution: ObjectInfo.position has no decision consumer outside Phase 4.
findings.required_change: Extend B3(c): oracle_phases=False also skips every update_object_positions call. Alternatively, define the override as a counted no-op and reword G16 to match. State whether D9 step (5) IS main()'s :562 settle (then the settle log and die-hidden assert need a declared B3 hook) or an extra settle (then B1(c) probes 100 steps).

findings.title: G5 fails on the lateral rediscovery cleanup, which the plan keeps unchanged
findings.plan_location: G5, G21, D6, B5, D1, B3, P4.8 KNOWN GAP, B7 GO criterion
findings.problem: Version 3 widens G5 to every SHADOW boxel, lateral or interior, that leaves the registry or the belief without a render of its grid. G5 names the rediscovery cleanup at execution.py:2871-2884 as 'exactly what this catches'. Yet D6 and B5 exempt only interior ids, and D1 and B3 keep that path unchanged for lateral fragments. Any arm-O episode in which a sense hits an already-registered cup inside a fragment therefore fails G5 and G21. This is likely in the 4-cup layouts, and B7's watched seed 1 uses one, so B7 has no defined outcome. The underlying defect is real: after reboxelize the removed area becomes free space and receives a Know-If not-here literal without any observation (an unsound belief write). The plan neither fixes it nor lists it beside the parked-fragment gap.
findings.evidence: execution.py:2871-2884 (registry.remove_boxel + belief.remove_shadow, no render); pddlstream_planner.py:675-681 (KIF on every free boxel); test_full_pipeline.py:1087-1097 (the F9 counter exists because rediscovery recurs); plan G5 text.
findings.required_change: Pre-register one option. Either (a) a main-pipeline fix that keeps superseded fragments unless _fragment_renders_empty, as retire_lost_objects does at execution.py:2105-2118, under the B3 acceptance with a BF#. Or (b) declare 'rediscovery re-cast' an enumerated, counted and disclosed channel in G5 and add it to P4.8's KNOWN GAP. Do not leave it as an unplanned gate failure.

findings.title: R6's 'the bridge passes the plan twin to the shadow raycaster' has no mechanism, and the raycast oracle is not gated
findings.plan_location: R6, B2 env_adapter (no override of boxel generation), B3, G2, G8(b)
findings.problem: All three shadow-casting call sites omit physics_client, so rayTestBatch runs on the default client. In the bridge that client is their executing world, which contains the hidden die. B2 forbids the adapter to override boxel generation, B3 lists no raycast-client parameter, and neither G2's grep nor G8(b)'s hooks include rayTest or rayTestBatch. Shadow extents end at the first body a ray hits. A die that is exposed but not yet registered (for example, occluded by the arm in the post-place render) would cut off a later re-cast fragment at its true position: a ground-truth read that feeds the belief while R6 claims it is gated. Pointing the caster at the plan twin also needs an ordering rule, because the initial generate_boxels runs before the first sync_to_plan_client.
findings.evidence: boxel_env.py:1512-1513; execution.py:2356-2357, 2979-2980; shadow_calculator.py:91-93, 160-173 (hits clamp the extent); sync_to_plan_client first runs inside the replanning loop (test_full_pipeline.py:1321), after Phase 2's boxelization (test_full_pipeline.py:610).
findings.required_change: B3 adds a shadow-raycast client parameter used at all three call sites, defaulting to None (thesis behaviour, so PAPER_AUDIT (h) stays as it is). The bridge sets it to the plan twin, synced to the just-estimated OBJECT boxes with every boxel-less body parked BEFORE each cast, including the initial generate_boxels. G2 adds rayTest and rayTestBatch, and G8(b) fails any ray call on the executing client from decision code.

findings.title: D9 calls itself complete but leaves out the object-side friction our grasp was validated with
findings.plan_location: D9 steps (3)-(4), G14 allowlist, B1(c), R8
findings.problem: Our validated friction grasp is pad 1.2 x object 1.0 (ObjectSpec's default lateral_friction 1.0, applied by changeDynamics). Their YCB bodies get no changeDynamics, so they keep PyBullet's 0.5, and the pad contact runs at mu 0.6. D9 sets only mass and inertia on task bodies and friction only on the pads, yet it is titled 'PRE-REGISTERED AND COMPLETE' and claims 'the values our executor's grasp is validated with'. G14 freezes D9's list. Any later friction change would therefore be chosen after seeing grasp failures in B7, which is the outcome-fitting R8 forbids.
findings.evidence: boxel_env.py:91 (lateral_friction 1.0), 674-677, 892-894, 802-812 (the mu 1.2 rationale); panda_env_utils.py:676-702 (no changeDynamics on YCB bodies).
findings.required_change: Decide before B1(c): either D9 step (3) also sets lateralFriction 1.0 on every task body, cited to ObjectSpec, or keeping 0.5 is pre-registered and disclosed. The B1(c) probe uses the same call.

findings.title: G6's 'beyond settle noise' leaves room for a post-hoc settle at the 1e-4 scoring boundary
findings.problem: Success turns on np.allclose(Q, DEFAULT_ARM_POS, 1e-4). G3 hooks motor commands but not stepSimulation, and the last POSITION_CONTROL targets keep driving the arm whenever the executing client is stepped. Stepping inside execute_fn after main() returns, before the observation is built, would converge the arm toward home with no planned action. It would pass G3. Whether it passes G6 depends on a 'settle noise' tolerance that the plan never defines, and a change of about 1e-4 is exactly the size of the score threshold.
findings.evidence: plan G6 text; find_dice env.py:318-321 (at-home test); robot_utils.py:754, 783 (position-control targets persist between steps).
findings.required_change: Count stepSimulation calls on the executing client after main() returns. The count must be 0 and goes into G21. The readback at main() return and the readback at observation build must be bit-identical.

findings.title: The G1, G3 and G14 trap lists miss the state-changing calls a 'nudge' would use
findings.problem: R7 names a nudge as the expected form of 'help'. None of the following is grepped or hooked: resetBaseVelocity, applyExternalForce, applyExternalTorque, resetJointStateMultiDof(s), setJointMotorControlMultiDof(Array), setCollisionFilterPair/Group (for example, filtering finger against cup or cup against die), changeConstraint, removeBody, and createMultiBody or loadURDF into the executing client. Each would pass G1, G3, G14 and G21. The main-pipeline modules use none of them. The archived bridge did call removeBody and create phantom bodies in their world.
findings.required_change: Add these calls to G1's grep and to G14's module-level trap (executing client, any task body or the robot), and add the MultiDof motor calls to G3's hook. No main-pipeline allowlist entry is needed today.

findings.title: B2's deliverable needs interior boxels, which only B5 implements
findings.plan_location: B2 deliverable vs B5, CALENDAR milestones
findings.problem: B2, due 2026-11-14, must 'build OBJECT, lateral and interior boxels from the first render'. Interior regions (region_kind, casting, the D6 status rule) are B5's work, due 2026-11-20. B2 cannot be accepted as written, or B5's model change would slip into the translation package without its own BF# and review.
findings.evidence: plan B2 'Deliverable' and B5 text; CALENDAR line 'B2 + B3 by 2026-11-14; B4-B6 by 2026-11-20'.
findings.required_change: B2 builds OBJECT and lateral boxels only. Interior boxels on seeds 0 and 1 become part of B5's deliverable.

findings.title: W has two definitions, and D6's version reads the released layouts
findings.plan_location: D6 STATUS RULE vs D8 / B1(e), R8, G9
findings.problem: D6 defines W as table cells 'whose column ... the t=0 render images unoccluded'. That is scene-dependent: it reads the released layout and would cut every cup's shadow out of W. D8 defines W from the EMPTY-table home render (frustum plus robot pixels), which is scene-independent, as R8 and the round-2 N8 fix require. Because W bounds free space, placements and the ShadowCalculator, the two readings give different belief models.
findings.evidence: plan D6 ('W contains only table cells whose column up to the tallest declared class height the t=0 render images unoccluded (D8, BF#2)') vs D8 ('free of robot pixels in the empty-table home render (B1(e))'); R8 'B1 decisions run on an empty table'.
findings.required_change: Rewrite D6's sentence to D8's empty-table definition. Leave the 'last imaged' record to supply the observational part.

findings.title: Two sections give different times for the honesty review gates
findings.problem: P4.1 says the adversarial pass runs on the B2+B3 diffs, then on B5, then on B7, each 'before the next package starts', so B2+B3 are reviewed before B4. B7 says 'The agent review of the B2+B3+B5+B6 diffs runs here'. Under that reading, B4 to B6 build on an unreviewed harness, and B6's constants are never reviewed under P4.1.
findings.evidence: plan P4.1 REVIEW GATES paragraph; B7 text.
findings.required_change: Keep P4.1's schedule: B2+B3 reviewed before B4, B5 before B6. Add B6 (the frozen constants and the D11 branch) to the review list, and correct B7's sentence.

findings.title: The calendar total disagrees with the per-package efforts
findings.problem: The listed efforts (B0 3, B1 2-3, B2 5-7, B3 4-5, B4 1-2, B5 3-4, B6 1-2 or up to 4 with M6, B7 3, B8 4) sum to 26 to 35 agent-days, not 27 to 34. With the review gates that is 29 to 38, not 30 to 37. The upper end exceeds the 35 calendar days by more than stated.
findings.required_change: Restate the totals as 26 to 35 and 29 to 38, and re-check the milestones and the latest B8 start against them.
